clue.text: Stress in past, for example, ultimately can make us nervous

parts.note: the past is one grammatical tense of a verb

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the four words that follow it

parts.note: the last letters of can, make, us and nervous

explanation.surface: Someone notes that putting the stress in a past utterance can unsettle us.
explanation.walkthrough: "for example" marks past as an instance of a tense; the four-word tail looks like the predicate but only lends its final letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenseness is a state of strain or nervous tension, which is what stress means as a noun.

clue.text: Gin perhaps beginning to sting mouths

parts.note: a gin is a snare for catching animals, one kind of trap

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the opening of sting is used

parts.note: the opening letter of sting

explanation.surface: Gin, it seems, starts to burn the drinker's mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin reads as the spirit, but here it is the old word for a snare. Trap is British slang for mouth, as in 'shut your trap'.
explanation.definitionFit: Trap is informal slang for a person's mouth, so traps is the plural for several speaking organs.

clue.text: Unaccompanied by deputy head of government at all events

parts.note: if you are not with someone you are unaccompanied by them
a stand-in deputises for someone

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the start of government counts

parts.note: the opening letter of government

explanation.surface: Someone acts without the deputy head of government, come what may.
explanation.walkthrough: "deputy head" looks like one title, but the deputy is separate and head belongs to government.
explanation.definitionFit: Notwithstanding as an adverb means nevertheless or in any case, the sense of the phrase at all events.

clue.text: Gull intrepid in pursuit of piece of cake

indicators.note: to be in pursuit is to come behind, so the word for intrepid follows the other piece

parts.note: something that is a piece of cake is easy
game as an adjective means brave and willing

explanation.surface: A daring seagull chases after a slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: Gull sounds like the seabird, but it means a dupe, someone easily fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: A gull is a gullible person, someone readily tricked, which is exactly what easy game means.

clue.text: Mistake made teen change for the better

indicators.note: a mistake puts things wrongly, so the letters that follow are taken in the wrong order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A teenager made an error, then reformed.
explanation.definitionFit: To emendate is to correct or improve a text, so it is to amend something for the better.

clue.text: Brilliant NFL game shunned by solemn type

indicators.note: something shunned is kept away, so the solemn type is removed from the game

parts.note: the Super Bowl is the championship game of American football's NFL
the owl is pictured as grave and solemn

explanation.surface: A dour person avoids watching the big American football final, though it was brilliant.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb and brilliant are both adjectives of high praise for something outstanding.

clue.text: Runs away from sullen elk

indicators.note: running away from something leaves it, so the runs letter leaves the word for sullen

parts.note: morose means sullen and gloomy
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An animal flees a sulky elk.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal called an elk in Britain is known as a moose in North America, the same deer.

clue.text: Half-forgotten homicide spooks Spanish city

indicators.note: if half is forgotten, only half of the word survives

parts.note: homicide is murder
spooks are spies, and the CIA is the US spy agency

explanation.surface: Spies investigate a half-remembered killing in a Spanish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Murcia is a city in south-eastern Spain, capital of the region of the same name.

clue.text: Senior citizen bats alongside opener

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so the following letters are scrambled

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly cricketer goes in to bat with the opening batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture makes bats a verb; it is the adjective meaning mad. An opener is a batsman who starts the innings.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-age pensioner is a retired person drawing a state pension, the British term for a senior citizen.

clue.text: Outgoing bonus cut? About time!

indicators.note: something cut is shortened, so the bonus word loses its last letter

parts.note: a bonus is something extra
over can mean about, as in a dispute over money
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone complains that it's about time their bonus was reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: "About time!" reads as an exclamation of impatience; here it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Outgoing describes a sociable, confident person, which is what an extrovert is, used here as an adjective.

clue.text: Entertainer coming out of Stuttgart is temperamental

indicators.note: the answer emerges from inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: found inside these three words

explanation.surface: A performer from the German city of Stuttgart is moody.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional performer, such as a singer or dancer, an entertainer by trade.

clue.text: Gemstone for every single girl

parts.note: per means for each
I is the Roman numeral one
Dot is a girl's name, short for Dorothy

explanation.surface: A jewel is promised to each unmarried young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Peridot is a green gem variety of the mineral olivine, used in jewellery.

clue.text: Cycling groups go in for wife-swapping

indicators.note: cycling moves letters round in a loop, so the last letter goes to the front

parts.note: wings are factions or groups within a party

explanation.surface: Bike-club members are into partner-swapping.
explanation.walkthrough: Cycling looks like the sport the groups do; it tells you to rotate the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Swinging is slang for the exchange of sexual partners between couples, so swing names that practice.

clue.text: Duke ordering rash acts of bravery

definitions.note: the answer is an uncountable noun for heroic action, the clue's phrase is plural

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke

indicators.note: a rash act is hasty and careless, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A nobleman orders reckless heroics.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is daring or heroic action, an old phrase for feats of courage.

clue.text: Two flyers, the first transfixed by opening of Hobbes' Leviathan

indicators.note: something transfixed is pierced through, so the first flyer has a letter stuck inside it

parts.note: the first of two flying insects

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so only the start of Hobbes is used

parts.note: the initial of Hobbes
the second flying insect

explanation.surface: Two winged creatures are spellbound by the start of Thomas Hobbes's political treatise Leviathan.
explanation.walkthrough: Leviathan reads as Hobbes's book, but it is the definition: a sea monster, hence anything huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Behemoth and leviathan are both biblical monsters, and each now means something enormous.

clue.text: Survival skills of husband trapped between vehicle and boat

indicators.note: something trapped between is held inside, so the husband letter sits within the vehicle word

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
a craft is a boat
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A man's wilderness know-how is tested when he is stuck between a bus and a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushcraft is the knowledge of how to live off the land in the wild, a set of survival techniques.

clue.text: People see oddly neglected Olympic event

indicators.note: neglecting the odd letters leaves only the even ones

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Spectators notice that an Olympic sport has been strangely ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Epee is one of the three fencing weapons and gives its name to an Olympic fencing discipline.

clue.text: Bug biting skin of heartbreakingly small body

indicators.note: biting holds something between the teeth, so the bug word closes around the other letters

parts.note: to bug someone is to annoy or pique them

indicators.note: a word's skin is its outer layer, its first and last letters

parts.note: the outer letters of heartbreakingly
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: An insect bites the skin of a tiny, pitiable body.
explanation.definitionFit: Physique is the form, size and build of a person's body.

clue.text: Capital Radio host interrupting call upset one

indicators.note: interrupting breaks into the middle of something, so the host sits inside the other letters

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns a word upside down, so the word for one reads backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one
a disc jockey hosts a radio show

explanation.surface: A presenter on the London station Capital Radio cuts in on a caller, who is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital Radio looks like the station's name; Capital is the definition and Radio host is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: N'Djamena is the capital city of Chad in central Africa.

clue.text: Takes skin test regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A patient undergoes allergy testing on the skin at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit an exam is to take it, so sits is the verb meaning takes in that sense.

clue.text: Harry Houdini leaving one in extremes of wonderment and mystery

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the outer pair
to harry is to harass and disturb, so the remaining letters are jumbled
leaving means departing, so the one letter departs from the name

parts.note: the escape artist's name, taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of wonderment

explanation.surface: Harry Houdini, the escapologist, leaves an audience full of wonder and puzzlement.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry looks like Houdini's first name, which it was; here it is the instruction to jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A whodunit is a detective story built around the puzzle of who committed a crime, a mystery novel.

clue.text: Kindly introduce golf into African country

indicators.note: to introduce something into a thing is to put it inside

parts.note: Benin is a country in West Africa
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A polite request to bring the game of golf to an African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Kindly reads as please, but it is the adjective meaning kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Benign and kindly are both adjectives describing a gentle, well-meaning nature.

clue.text: Hill is start of Appalachian trail

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of Appalachian
a scent is a trail followed by hounds

explanation.surface: A slope marks where the Appalachian Trail hiking route begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The Appalachian Trail is a famous long-distance footpath, which hides that trail is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is an upward slope, so a hill can be called one, as in a steep climb.

clue.text: Unanimity of statisticians taking part in survey

indicators.note: taking part in something means being inside it, so the statisticians go within the survey word

parts.note: a census is an official survey of a population
the ONS is Britain's Office for National Statistics

explanation.surface: Statisticians conducting a survey all agree.
explanation.definitionFit: Consensus is general agreement among a group, which is what unanimity means.

clue.text: Silly answer meeting sanctimonious silence

indicators.note: meeting means coming up against, so the first letter is placed directly next to the pieces that follow

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
pi is informal British for pious or sanctimonious
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A foolish reply is met with a self-righteous hush.
explanation.definitionFit: Apish means behaving like an ape, so foolish or affectedly imitative.

clue.text: Utter confusion for US president

indicators.note: to utter is to say out loud, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a haze is a state of mental confusion

explanation.surface: Total bewilderment about an American president.
explanation.walkthrough: Utter looks like the adjective meaning total; it is the verb meaning to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Rutherford B. Hayes was the nineteenth President of the United States, from 1877 to 1881.

clue.text: Drunk is inane and idiotic

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady and muddled, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk person is silly and foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means extremely stupid or foolish, like a donkey, so it is a synonym of idiotic.

clue.text: Royal, mostly odd, however, deprived of love

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the odd word loses its last letter
deprived of something means without it, so the love letter is removed from the however word

parts.note: queer in its older sense means odd or strange
only can mean however, as in 'I'd come, only I'm busy'
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A royal figure is described as rather peculiar, yet lacking in love.
explanation.definitionFit: Queenly means befitting a queen, regal, so it serves as an adjective meaning royal.

clue.text: Cross old so-and-so retired with grin at last

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the so-and-so word is read backwards

parts.note: git is British slang for an unpleasant person, a so-and-so
O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of grin

parts.note: the final letter of grin

explanation.surface: An angry old pensioner finally grins.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross looks like the adjective for angry; it is the noun for a hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigon is the hybrid offspring of a male tiger and a lioness, a cross between two big cats.

clue.text: Giving away tips, these dons sign book

indicators.note: to don is to put on, as clothing, so the sign wraps around the other letters
giving away the tips means losing both end letters of the word

parts.note: taken as written
Taurus is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: University lecturers reveal secrets as they sign a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Dons look like academics here, and tips like hints; dons is the verb meaning puts on.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a reference book listing words grouped by similar meaning.
